question: Is familial paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, which means one copy of the altered gene in each cell is typically sufficient to cause the disorder. Almost everyone with a mutation in the PNKD gene will develop familial paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia. In all reported cases, an affected person has inherited the mutation from one parent.
greedy_answer:
Familial paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia (FPND) is a rare genetic disorder. It is indeed inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern. This means that a mutation in one of the two copies of the gene is sufficient to cause the condition. 

The condition is caused by mutations in the PRRT2 gene, which is responsible for encoding a protein that plays a crucial role in the regulation of neurotransmitter release in the brain. The mutations in this gene can lead to abnormal neuronal activity, resulting in the symptoms of FPND.

FPND is characterized by sudden, brief episodes of involuntary movements, such as dystonic postures, chorea, or athetosis, which can occur at any time, without any apparent trigger or warning. The episodes can be triggered by stress, fatigue, or other factors, but they can also occur spontaneously.

The inheritance pattern of FPND means that if one parent has the condition, each child has a 50% chance of inheriting the mutated gene and developing the condition.
